Your data stays on your device
Decks, cards, review history, media and settings are stored only in the app's private storage. There is no Mnemo account and no Mnemo server. Backups and exports go only where you choose.
Mnemo contains no analytics, advertising or crash-reporting code, and collects nothing about how you use it.

If you add an AI provider, the text you ask about (a source for Smart Extract, a card for Explain or Rewrite, or a deck's cards for Co-Author) is sent directly from your device to that provider, after you confirm it once. Its privacy policy applies to what it receives. If you report an AI answer, Mnemo only opens a draft in your browser with that answer. Nothing is sent until you submit it there.
Keys are encrypted with a key held by the system (the Android keystore on a phone, the keychain on a computer), never included in backups or exports, and never logged.

Internet: only for AI providers and links you open in Smart Extract. A phone also asks for Notifications (reminders and progress of long imports) and, only while you dictate, the Microphone (speech is recognized on your device where it can be). A computer asks for no permissions.
Off. Keep your devices in step through storage you own.
Paused after a restore. Choose what to do.
On. Waiting to reach the sync location.

Mnemo has no server. Each device writes its changes as files to a place you own (a folder you choose, a WebDAV server such as Nextcloud or, where this version offers it, your Google Drive) and reads the other devices' files from it, so the decks, notes and reviews of all your devices end up together, also when you studied offline.

What is stored there: your decks, notes, review history, images and scheduling settings, in files that only Mnemo reads. AI providers, API keys, appearance and the reminder stay on each device. Mnemo has no server and never sees these files; they go only where you put them.
The folder can be inside Google Drive, Dropbox, Nextcloud or Syncthing: that app then carries the files to your other computers.
Pick an empty folder, or make a new one. A sync app such as Syncthing or Nextcloud can carry it to your other devices.
Mnemo keeps its files in a hidden folder of your Google Drive that only Mnemo can open. It can't see anything else in your Drive. The files count against your Drive storage.
